description: This search gives up to `k` paths from a start to a goal that overlap little. It ranks loopless paths best-first by a scalar cost, with ties broken by the edge sequence, and keeps a path only if it shares at most `max_shared` edges with every path it kept before. The answer is greedy: each kept path is the cheapest one that is different enough from the earlier ones, not the best set as a whole. It needs a graph with edge identities (`EdgeGraph`), and its run time can grow exponentially, as for every ranking method. Use it to offer alternative routes, or backup routes that do not fail together.

papers.authors: Ali Moghanni, Marta Pascoal, Maria Teresa Godinho
papers.title: Finding shortest and dissimilar paths
